claims.reason: Backed: the number serves for login and recovery and a Google account change does not reach every service (Korzyść i dowody#1), and a new number may need time before it can verify sensitive actions (line 13). Not backed by any snapshot: the instruction to test the new number or method, the ordering 'before you lose access' as a rule (no snapshot describes what happens if the old number is lost first), and 'inną metodę odzyskiwania' for services other than Google (the Google region speaks only of a backup phone number; NCSC mentions 2SV by SMS or email but no alternative to a phone number).

claims.reason: The Google snapshot is the provider's own help page. The grade letter C is editorial and was not checked. The second cited source (NCSC, UK government guidance) is not provider documentation and is not described by this sentence.

Searched both cited snapshots for any study, trial, data or estimate of losses avoided or prevented; both are help or guidance text with no such study. Absence is only from the stored main regions (Google 5181 of 9057 chars, NCSC 6804 of 9603 chars), not from the whole pages.

scope_gaps.note: The Google page describes adding, changing or removing a number on a Google account, not giving up the number itself (cancelling or losing the SIM). Giving up the number is the advice's premise, not something the source measured.

Source facts concern Google account and Google services only. Testing the new method, doing it before losing the old number, and alternatives to a phone number for other providers are not in any snapshot.

The NCSC lines used (email and banking priority, per-provider recovery procedure, updating bank sites with new details) come from UK guidance on recovering a hacked account, not on phone number changes; Google line 61 covers only Google services.
Google states non-propagation only for Google services; extension to all services and providers is by analogy.

The statement concerns a Google account and Google services. A reader might assume the same holds for banks, email from other providers and other services; the sentence does not say so. The Polish page carries a notice that it may be AI-translated (line 125).
The justification is direct only for Google services; for other providers it rests on analogy, which Ograniczenia#2 and #3 acknowledge.
The item cites the NCSC page (UK government guidance) as a second source, but the evidence description names only provider documentation and an editorial checklist.
